messages:
marie: quick RFC follow-up re: splitting dashboard render into fast/slow lanes. goal is lower p99 for small widgets while keeping correctness for complex queries. want to align on where RBAC lives, cache eviction, and fallback semantics. thoughts? :thinking:

aj: big +1 on lowering p99. my main worry: if we do lightweight auth in fastpath we risk serving stale perms. how do we guarantee eventual correctness?

marie: right. proposal sketch: do a cheap capability check in fastpath (cached token) that gates display, then enqueue authoritative permission check in slowpath that can invalidate cached tile and trigger re-render if mismatch. fastpath should be allowed to show a placeholder or degraded widget until auth confirmed.

sam: from SRE ops perspective we need audit logs for the authoritative check and a clear TTL for capability cache. otherwise a rolling permission change could be invisible for minutes. also watch the write amplification for invalidations.

lee: runtime note: continuous batching and KV cache already give us hooks for prefix-level invalidation. we could attach a lease id to cached tiles and keep a small heartbeat to mark liveness. if authoritative check fails, we bump lease and push invalidation message to the invalidation topic.

nina: sketch of header / token flow i mentioned in the RFC spike:

```
# fastpath request from frontend -> gateway
GET /dash/widgets?user=U1
Host: console.internal
X-Capability: cap_v1:widget-read:abc123;ttl=30s
Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-client-token>
```

nina: capability token is minted by auth service on login/change and is kept short (15-60s). gateway validates signature and TTL cheaply, runtime uses cap to decide which cached tile to serve.

aj: +1 but two followups: 1) who mints the cap on permission change? 2) what if cap remains valid but authoritative store says access removed? need deterministic fallback UX.

marie: answers: 1) auth service mints on session start and on explicit permission change events it revokes/mints new caps. 2) fallback UX = show blurred/locked widget with CTA to refresh. also emit telemetry event so product can track.

sam: add ops constraints: invalidation messages must be idempotent and rate-limited. would rather queue coalesced invalidations per-tenant. otherwise burst from a permission sweep kills broker.

lee: implementation detail: lease id as vector: <tenant>-<tile-hash>-<lease-counter>. On authoritative invalidation we increment lease-counter and write to invalidation log. runtime can fast-path check lease value without calling authz store often.

nina: tradeoff: keeping lease metadata increases cache entry size but avoids synchronous authz calls on every fastpath hit. we should quantify memory vs saved RPCs in benchmark.

marie: can someone spike perf numbers and a simple PoC of lease-based invalidation? suggested owners: lee + nina. please include a small loadtest for permission-sweep scenario.

lee: i'll take the PoC. estimating 2d. will push a branch and ping here.

nina: i'll own the auth changes and revocation flow. will prototype cap mint/revoke endpoints.

deploy-bot: marie requested a spike branch: spike/fastpath-lease-poc created (PR #487). :white_check_mark:

aj: one more thought on UX: degraded widget should have stable dimensions to avoid layout shifts. product asked for that in past.

marie: good call. add to spike acceptance: stable layout + telemetry. also we need a small doc paragraph on security model (capabilities are not full authz). i'll draft.

sam: FYI ops, i'll add a runbook for sweeping invalidation and broker backpressure mitigation.

marie: thanks all. next sync Fri 11am. if anything else pops up, drop notes here. :eyes:
